A genuine Rekor v2 entry whose verifier is a certificate — complete, and
verified end to end by this build's own client.

Published 2026-08-16 to https://log2025-1.rekor.sigstore.dev (HTTP 201
Created, logIndex 68295246). Nothing in this repository authored the log's
half of any of it: not the checkpoint, not its signature lines, not the tree
the audit path walks.

  statement.json           452 B  the in-toto Statement, byte-exact — the
                                  DSSE PAE preimage the leaf's digest commits
                                  to. Keeping it is what makes this fixture
                                  total (see "what this proves").
  certificate.der         1118 B  the entry's verifier, extracted from
                                  spec.hashedRekordV002.signature.verifier
                                    .x509Certificate.rawBytes.
  canonicalized_body.json 1863 B  the Merkle leaf preimage, verbatim, as the
                                  log returned it.
  checkpoint.txt           643 B  the signed note the log returned with the
                                  entry. It carries FOUR signature lines: the
                                  log's own Ed25519 signature plus three
                                  witness cosignatures. Nothing here
                                  interprets a cosignature, but the parser has
                                  to tolerate them — narrowing it to a single
                                  signature would reject every checkpoint the
                                  production log serves, and this file is the
                                  regression test for that.
  proof.bin               3454 B  the encoded RekorProof record — the exact
                                  bytes a zone serves at
                                  _synchronicity-rekor.<apex>.
  anchor.txt               144 B  the DNSSEC trust anchor this zone is under.
  log_index.txt                   68295246.

The entry is a `rollover` for zone-key-transparency.demo.invalid, key tag
32784. Its chain carries the zone's transparency declaration at
_synchronicity-transparency.<apex> and proves that key under it, so a monitor
holding the anchor above classifies it tier A — an authorization — and reports
it the first time it sees it. That is what crates/synch-monitor/tests/
real_entry.rs asserts, and crates/synch-net/tests/rekor_zone_key.rs runs the
whole client verifier over the same bytes.

WHAT THIS PROVES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT

It proves interoperability with the real log: that Rekor v2 accepts a
self-signed certificate as a hashedrekord verifier with no chain validation of
any kind, that an 1118-byte certificate carrying a custom extension under the
narrowed 2.25 arc is accepted, that the returned inclusion proof and
checkpoint verify under the log key this build embeds, and that the whole
record round-trips through the wire form a zone actually serves — and then
verifies, unmodified, through the client's own path.

It does NOT prove real-world DNSSEC chain validation. The chain in this
certificate is SELF-ANCHORED: the apex is its own trust anchor, because no
DNSSEC-signed domain was available to publish under, and minting a certificate
naming a domain we do not control would be squatting a name in a permanent
public log. A monitor anchored at the ICANN root therefore classifies this
entry tier B, correctly — it cannot tell whether the key was authorized.
ICANN-rooted validation is the job of the separate fixture in
../dnssec_chain/, captured from live DNS for cloudflare.com, which exercises
RSASHA256 at the root and ECDSAP256SHA256 below it.

REGENERATING

Publishing is a permanent, public, irreversible write. Do it only when the
entry format changes in a way that invalidates these bytes, and keep the SAN
under .invalid so no real name is claimed:

  SYNCH_REKOR_PUBLISH=yes-write-to-the-real-log cargo test -p synch-net \
    --test rekor_zone_key -- --ignored --nocapture publish_a_real_entry

It mints a fresh zone key, submits the entry, verifies what comes back
through the full client verifier, and only then rewrites these files.
Afterwards the pinned constants in crates/synch-net/tests/rekor_zone_key.rs
(LOG_INDEX, KEY_TAG, certificate length) and crates/synch-monitor/tests/
real_entry.rs (LOG_INDEX, key tag, DS prefix) all have to move with it.
